cards.text: Last time, Joseph settled his family in a town called Nazareth. Now a preacher named John the Baptist shows up, preaching in the wilderness of Judea. No stage, no building, just John and a whole lot of nothing.

cards.question: John the Baptist's message is short: the kingdom of heaven is near. So what does he tell people to do?

cards.text: Matthew says John is the one the prophet Isaiah spoke of long ago: "A voice of one calling in the wilderness." Friend, John showed up right on cue. I can't even show up on cue to my own oven timer.

cards.question: In Isaiah's words, the voice in the wilderness calls people to prepare something. What is it?

cards.text: Now let's talk about John's outfit. Because this man did NOT dress up for the crowd.

cards.question: John wears a garment of ___ hair, with a leather belt around his waist.
Out in the wilderness, what does John the Baptist eat?

cards.text: Locusts and wild honey. Friend, that's not a menu, that's a DARE. And you'd think nobody would walk all the way out to the wilderness to hear the guy in camel hair.

cards.question: Only a few people go out to the wilderness to hear John the Baptist.
The people who come to John are baptized by him in the Jordan River while confessing their sins.

cards.text: Then John sees many of the Pharisees and Sadducees, two groups of Jewish religious leaders, coming to where he's baptizing. I bet the whole riverbank went quiet.

cards.question: When John sees the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his place of baptism, what does he call them?

cards.text: Not "good morning." Not "welcome." Straight to SNAKES. Then John asks them, "who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?"

cards.question: John tells the Pharisees and Sadducees to produce ___ in keeping with repentance.

cards.text: Then John shuts down an excuse before anybody can even say it out loud. That's like me answering "the oven was too hot" before anyone asks about the burnt batch.

cards.question: John warns the Pharisees and Sadducees not to count on having Abraham as their father.
John says that out of these ___, God can raise up children for Abraham.

cards.text: Then John paints a picture. The axe lies ready at the root of the trees.

cards.question: In John's picture of the axe at the root, what happens to every tree that doesn't produce good fruit?

answers.text: It is cut down and thrown into the fire
It is dug around and given another year
It is left standing alone in the field

cards.text: Now John the Baptist talks about Someone who will come after him. And this is where it gets good, friend.

cards.question: John says the One coming after him is less powerful than he is.
John says he isn't even worthy to do what for the One coming after him?

cards.text: John is the one baptizing everybody, and he says he's not worthy to carry this Man's SANDALS. Meanwhile, I stamp ONE straight cookie and I want a parade.

cards.question: John baptizes with water for repentance. What does he say the One coming after him will baptize with?

cards.text: Then John paints a harvest picture. The One coming has His winnowing fork in His hand, ready to clear His threshing floor.

cards.question: In John's harvest picture, the One coming will gather His ___ into the barn, but He will burn up the ___ with unquenchable fire.

cards.text: At that time, Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan, right where John is.

cards.question: Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.

cards.text: But John tries to stop Him. I think John is standing in that river wondering if this is really happening.

cards.question: When John tries to stop Jesus from being baptized, what does John say?

answers.text: I need to be baptized by You
The river is too deep today
You must go back to Galilee

cards.text: Jesus answers him, "Let it be so now," and then, "It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way."

cards.question: After Jesus answers, John still refuses to baptize Him.

cards.text: As soon as Jesus is baptized, He goes up out of the water. And SUDDENLY, the heavens are opened.

cards.question: Jesus sees the Spirit of God descending like a ___ and resting on Him.

cards.text: Like a dove, friend, and my Minty is shaped like a dove, so you KNOW I lean in close every time I read this. Then a voice from heaven speaks.

cards.question: After Jesus comes up out of the Jordan, what does the voice from heaven say?

answers.text: This is My beloved Son in whom I am well pleased
This is My chosen servant who will rule the nations
This is the prophet who will lead My people home

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 3 quotes "A voice of one calling in the wilderness.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card starts with 'Last time, Joseph settled his family in a town called Nazareth.' That fact comes from the previous passage (Matthew 2:23), which is context only. The passage has no story group, and the line assumes the baker did an earlier lesson. The card also cites only Matthew 3:1 while stating a fact from Matthew 2:23.

rule.text: The passage right before it is also provided, for context only. It is not part of the lesson.

findings.problem: The card states a fact from Matthew 2:23 but cites only Matthew 3:1.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 3 quotes Isaiah's line up to 'calling in the wilderness.' Card 4 then asks what comes next in the quote ('Prepare the way for the Lord'). That is guessing the next words of a line, not reasoning about meaning. 'Calls people to prepare' also names an audience the text leaves open.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The setup 'you'd think nobody would walk all the way out to the wilderness' signals the opposite. That gives away the answer (False) to the true or false card that follows.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says people went out 'to hear John the Baptist' (card 8 says 'to hear the guy in camel hair'). Matthew 3:5 says only that people went out to him. It gives no reason, and 3:6 says they were baptized confessing their sins.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: In John's excuse, the core action is John ruling out an excuse other people might make. The comparison has Papa Dorin making his own excuse early. The actions don't match.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Abraham shows up for the first time (cards 15 to 17) with no simple line saying who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: About half of stop 1's 11 choice cards can't be reasoned out from earlier cards: card 4 (next words of Isaiah's line), card 6 (camel hair), card 7 (locusts and wild honey), card 12 (brood of vipers) and card 17 (stones). Cards 6 and 7 come back to back with almost no setup. That is more than a few discovery questions.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Jesus appears for the first time in the passage with no simple line saying who He is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'The river is too deep today' is silly, and it doesn't match the tone or kind of the right answer. The right answer is a humble statement about who should baptize whom.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
